## Open

### F-257 — p-queue hands the task its own options where there is no test context

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong-chain · open_

The per-step function in the executor receives a second argument that is a test context only when
the caller supplied one: with no testContext the step runs through queue.add(fn), and p-queue calls
fn with its task options, so the argument is not undefined but an object carrying a signal. A new
code path guarded on it being non-undefined, called context.test on those options, and threw at the
first step that announced progress (progress.test.ts caught it). The snapshot code beside it already
had the rule: check typeof context.test === function, never for undefined.

### F-260 — Awaiting a step that failed hangs instead of rejecting

> _2026-09-25 · core/blong-chain · open_

A step that awaits a step which failed never settles, so the failure surfaces as a timeout rather
than as the error. Observed in the handler-test-poc scenarios: a named login step whose call threw
(server answered 500) left the dependent createOrder waiting until the runner timeout, about 25
seconds, reported only as timeout. The executor catch path does call promiseManager.reject for the
failed step, so the rejection is either not reaching the promise the dependent step holds, or is
created for a different key. Worth chasing: failing fast with the message costs nothing, and a hang
hides the reason and multiplies the run length by the number of scenarios.

### F-283 — The examples leg read a dist/ that noEmit stopped producing

> _2026-09-26 · core/blong-chain · open_

`ci-test` is `blong-dev test '*.test.ts';./test-examples-ci.sh`, and that second half had been
failing since `fb730360` changed this package's tsconfig to the repo convention —
`allowImportingTsExtensions` requires it — which added `noEmit: true`. `heft build --clean` deletes
`dist` and emits nothing, so `node --test dist/examples/*.test.js` found zero tests and the script
reported every expected pattern missing, plus "Example tests should have failures but all passed".
The examples were written for a compiled world twice over: the script looked in `dist/`, and the
files imported `'../index.js'` and `'../test-types.js'`. They run from source now, as everything
else in the repo does: `test:examples` is `node --test examples/*.test.ts`, the imports name the
`.ts` files, and the two headers' run instructions match. Verified by the script itself (all
patterns found) and by `ci-test` exiting 0. Worth knowing for the next failure of this shape: the CI
report's Result column is built from the runner's counts, so a failing shell half of a package's
`ci-test` shows as a green package while `rush ci-test` is returning non-zero, and nothing in the
published report says so.
